content: Sulfa allergies are adverse reactions to medications that contain sulfonamides. It is crucial to understand that the absence of the word sulfa in a medication's name does not guarantee that the drug is free of sulfonamides. This is particularly relevant when considering generic drug names. Antibiotics that contain sulfonamides and may trigger allergic reactions include sulfamethoxazole, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (commonly known as Septra or Bactrim), and erythromycin-sulfisoxazole. Individuals with a sulfonamide allergy should also avoid medications closely related to sulfonamides, such as sulfasalazine (Azulfidine) and dapsone. There are additional medications related to sulfonamides that should be used with caution in individuals with a sulfa allergy. Although the risk of an allergic reaction is significantly lower with these drugs, it is essential to consult a healthcare provider to carefully evaluate the risks and benefits. These medications include: Diuretics, such as furosemide (Lasix) and hydrochlorothiazide (Microzide). Certain diabetes medications, such as glyburide (Glynase, Diabeta, Micronase) and glimepiride (Amaryl). Specific nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), such as celecoxib (Celebrex). Migraine treatments, such as sumatriptan (Imitrex). Patients with HIV/AIDS may exhibit increased sensitivity to sulfonamides or medications with similar chemical structures. However, it is important to note that sulfites and sulfates, which are commonly used as food preservatives, are unlikely to cause adverse reactions in individuals with a sulfa allergy.
